questions.q: Why is a page that only says "HighErrorRate firing for checkout-api" not enough on its own?
options: Alertmanager does not allow any additional text in a notification
It tells the responder that something is wrong but gives no diagnosis steps, known fixes, or escalation path to act on
Error rate alerts are always false positives
PagerDuty strips all alert labels before delivering a page
questions.explain: A bare alert name tells you something is wrong but not what to do about it — that's exactly the gap a runbook is meant to close.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what four things belong in a real runbook?
options: A full architecture diagram, a cost breakdown, a changelog, and a list of every engineer who ever touched the service
Only a link to the service's source code repository
A severity tier, a Slack channel name, and nothing else
What the alert means, first diagnosis steps, known fixes, and an escalation path
questions.explain: The lesson's structure is: plain-language meaning, specific diagnosis steps in order, fixes that have actually worked before, and who to escalate to if unresolved.

questions.q: What does the `runbook_url` annotation on a Prometheus alert rule do?
options: It attaches a runbook link directly to the alert rule so it travels through Alertmanager into every notification channel automatically
It deletes the alert after the runbook is opened
It is a required field with no functional effect on notifications
It silences the alert until someone clicks the link
questions.explain: Setting runbook_url as an annotation means the link rides along with the alert into Slack, PagerDuty, or email, sitting right next to the page itself.

questions.q: How does a runbook differ from a postmortem?
options: A runbook is written after an incident; a postmortem is written before one
They are the same document under two different names
A runbook is prepared ahead of time as a how-to-respond for a known failure mode; a postmortem is written after a specific incident to analyze what happened and drive follow-up work
Only postmortems can be linked from an alert annotation
questions.explain: A runbook stays mostly static between incidents as a prepared response guide; a postmortem is retrospective and specific to one occurrence.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say a team that only writes postmortems and never turns a recurring one into a runbook keeps re-learning the same lesson?
options: Postmortems are automatically deleted after 30 days
Because the knowledge from each postmortem stays as a one-off record instead of being attached to the alert for the next responder to use immediately
Because postmortems cannot contain diagnosis steps by definition
Because Alertmanager requires a runbook_url to even fire an alert
questions.explain: Without converting a recurring incident's known cause and fix into a runbook linked from the alert, the next responder starts from zero again even though the team has already solved this exact problem before.
